Stages of classify_duplicates()

Source: R/utils-classify.R
resolve_classification_cols.Rd

Internal helpers that classify_duplicates() runs in order, so the exported function reads as a short pipeline.

Usage

resolve_classification_cols(data_clean, call = rlang::caller_env())

resolve_patient_class_col(data_clean, verbose)

summarize_visit_groups(
  data_clean,
  fac_col_str,
  visit_col_str,
  cols,
  patient_class,
  verbose
)

classify_dup_type(visit_groups, has_patient_class)

summarize_dup_by_facility(dup_rows, fac_col_str)

summarize_dup_overall(dup_rows)

Arguments

data_clean

A data frame already passed through clean_names_safe().

call

The environment errors are attributed to; see resolve_col().

verbose

Logical. Whether to emit informational messages.

fac_col_str, visit_col_str

Names of the facility and visit columns.

cols

The list returned by resolve_classification_cols().

patient_class

The list returned by resolve_patient_class_col().

visit_groups

The data frame returned by summarize_visit_groups().

has_patient_class

Logical. Whether C_Patient_Class is available.

dup_rows

visit_groups restricted to rows whose dup_type is not "no_duplication".

Value

resolve_classification_cols() returns a list with biosense, date, and pid (strings). resolve_patient_class_col() returns a list with has_patient_class and pc_col_str. summarize_visit_groups() and classify_dup_type() return the visit-group data frame (the latter with dup_type). summarize_dup_by_facility() and summarize_dup_overall() return tibbles.

Details

The stages, in the order classify_duplicates() calls them:

  1. resolve_classification_cols() resolves the three required columns (C_BioSense_ID, Date, C_Unique_Patient_ID), accepting raw ESSENCE names, janitor::clean_names() output, or variants, and aborts listing every missing one.

  2. resolve_patient_class_col() resolves the optional C_Patient_Class column; without it patient class change detection is skipped.

  3. summarize_visit_groups() collapses data to one row per facility x visit group with the number of distinct C_BioSense_IDs, dates, patient identifiers, and patient classes. A missing facility_col or visit_col value means that row's true identity is unknown, not confirmed to match every other row with a missing value, so it is grouped with na_safe_group_id() rather than dplyr::group_by() (which would treat every NA as equal and silently classify unrelated visits as duplicated).

  4. classify_dup_type() assigns the dup_type from which fields varied: "no_duplication" for a single row, "type_unknown" for several rows with no variation in the assessed fields, one of the three single mechanisms, or a compound of two or three joined with +.

  5. summarize_dup_by_facility() and summarize_dup_overall() build the two summary tables from the rows classified as duplicates. summarize_dup_overall() builds the empty tibble directly for a clean pull, because janitor::adorn_pct_formatting() errors on a 0-row tabyl (it tries to write a "%" string into a 0-row percent column).
